title: Korhonen–Lokshtanov Question on Induced Disjoint Paths in Induced-Minor-Free Classes
statement_text: Is Induced $k$-Disjoint Paths NP-hard in $H$-induced-minor-free graphs for some fixed $k$ and $H$?
context_text: Korhonen and Lokshtanov posed this question to understand the tractability frontier of Induced $k$-Disjoint Paths when graphs are restricted by excluding a fixed induced minor. The problem is NP-complete in general graphs for $k=2$ but polynomial in planar and bounded-genus graphs, leaving the induced-minor-free setting open.
paper_contribution: Resolves the question affirmatively for $k=2$ and $H$ equal to the 1-subdivision of $K_{5}$ (or $K_{3,3}$): Induced 2-Disjoint Paths (and the stronger Induced Disjoint $S$–$T$ Paths with $|S|=|T|=2$) is NP-complete in string graphs, which exclude every 1-subdivision of a non-planar graph as an induced minor.
paper_title: Induced Disjoint Paths Without an Induced Minor

title: Chudnovsky–Seymour–Trotignon Question on Subcubic Induced Subdivision Containment
statement_text: Is there a subcubic graph $H$ such that deciding whether an input graph contains $H$ as an induced subdivision ($H$-\textsc{ISC}) is NP-complete?
context_text: Until this paper, every graph $H$ for which $H$-ISC was known to be NP-complete had a vertex of degree at least 4. Chudnovsky, Seymour, and Trotignon (the fourth author of the present paper) asked whether NP-hardness of induced subdivision containment can occur for subcubic graphs.
paper_contribution: Answers the question affirmatively: by leveraging the NP-completeness of Induced 2-Disjoint Paths in string graphs (Theorem 1.1), the paper exhibits a fixed subcubic graph $H$ for which $H$-ISC is NP-complete (Theorems 1.3–1.4).

title: Conjecture 1.5
statement_text: For any subcubic graph $H$, $H$-\textsc{ISC} is in $\mathsf{P}$ if and only if $H$ is planar.
context_text: A subcubic graph has maximum degree at most 3. $H$ is an induced subdivision of $G$ if some subdivision of $H$ (obtained by replacing edges by paths) is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of $G$; $H$-ISC ($H$-Induced Subdivision Containment), for fixed $H$, takes a graph $G$ as input and asks whether $H$ is an induced subdivision of $G$. The conjecture is stated under the assumption $\mathsf{P}\neq\mathsf{NP}$. Polynomial algorithms are known for several planar $H$: $K_{2,3}$ (via Chudnovsky and Seymour's Three-In-A-Tree algorithm), the net (a triangle with a pendant vertex at each vertex), $K_4$, and disjoint unions of a fixed number of triangles; $K_5$ and some trees give NP-complete cases. Chudnovsky, Seymour, Trotignon and Le asked whether $H$-ISC is polynomial for every subcubic $H$. The paper answers this negatively, exhibiting a 66-vertex non-planar subcubic graph $H$ (built from 1-subdivisions of $K_{3,3}$) for which $H$-ISC is NP-complete; the proof derives from the NP-completeness of Induced 2-Disjoint Paths (finding two mutually induced paths between two given terminal pairs) in string graphs, which exclude the 1-subdivision of every non-planar graph as an induced minor. The conjecture proposes that planarity is exactly the dividing line among subcubic graphs.
notes: The 'only if' direction (NP-hardness for non-planar subcubic $H$) implicitly assumes $\mathsf{P}\neq\mathsf{NP}$.

title: Informal Question on Complexity Gap Between Induced Disjoint Paths Variants
statement_text: Is there a hereditary graph class in which Induced $k$-Disjoint Paths is NP-complete but Induced Disjoint $S$–$T$ Paths with $|S|=|T|=k$ is polynomial-time solvable? The case $k=2$ is of particular interest.
context_text: In Induced $k$-Disjoint Paths (the linkage variant) one is given a graph $G$ and $k$ terminal pairs $(s_1,t_1),\dots,(s_k,t_k)$ and asks for paths $P_1,\dots,P_k$, $P_i$ joining $s_i$ to $t_i$, that are mutually induced, i.e. $G[\bigcup_i V(P_i)]$ is exactly the disjoint union of the paths (they are vertex-disjoint and no edge of $G$ joins two of them). In Induced Disjoint $S$–$T$ Paths (the flow variant) one is given disjoint sets $S,T\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|=|T|$ and asks for $|S|$ mutually induced paths each with one end in $S$ and the other in $T$. Without the induced requirement both problems are polynomial (Robertson–Seymour, respectively Menger's theorem); the induced variants are NP-complete in general for $k=2$ and $|S|=|T|=2$. Induced Disjoint $S$–$T$ Paths with $|S|=|T|=k$ reduces to $k!$ calls of Induced $k$-Disjoint Paths, so for constant $k$ it is in principle easier. The authors observe that the polynomial algorithms in the literature (planar graphs, bounded genus, bounded mim-width, claw-free graphs, (theta, wheel)-free graphs) tend to apply to Induced $k$-Disjoint Paths, while hardness proofs, including theirs for string graphs (intersection graphs of curves in the plane) of bounded degree and twin-width, tend to apply already to Induced Disjoint $S$–$T$ Paths with $|S|=|T|=k$. A hereditary class is one closed under taking induced subgraphs.
